name: hilbert_encode
description: Encode coordinates into one unsigned integer using the Hilbert curve. Pass a fixed-size array, or two or more separate arguments cast to their common type. Accepts 8–64-bit integers, FLOAT and DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, DECIMAL (up to 18 digits) and ENUM, with at most 128 combined bits. Keys sort like the coordinates, including negative and floating-point values.

examples.description: Order nonnegative integer coordinates by their Hilbert curve key
Pass coordinates as separate arguments, including negative values
Encode two dates

name: hilbert_decode
description: Recover coordinates from a Hilbert curve key. Name the encoded type: hilbert_decode(key, 'DOUBLE[2]'), 'DATE[2]', or a scalar type for one dimension. The original form takes the dimension count and (return_float, return_unsigned): (false, true) for unsigned integers, (false, false) for signed integers, (true, false) for floats. Signedness must match the encoded values. Preserve the key's SQL type.

examples.description: Decode into a named type
Decode dates
examples.code:
SELECT d[1] AS first_date, d[2] AS second_date
FROM (SELECT hilbert_decode(hilbert_encode(DATE '2024-03-01', DATE '1965-07-04'), 'DATE[2]') AS d);

examples.description: Original form: num_elements, return_float, return_unsigned
examples.code: SELECT hilbert_decode(hilbert_encode([10, 20]::UINTEGER[2]), 2, false, true) AS roundtrip;

examples.description: Signed integers need return_unsigned = false
examples.code: SELECT hilbert_decode(hilbert_encode([-10, 20]::INTEGER[2]), 2, false, false) AS roundtrip;

name: hilbert_encode_bounded
description: Scale each DOUBLE coordinate from [min, max] onto a grid of 2^bits cells and encode the cell with the Hilbert curve. Returns the narrowest unsigned integer that holds dimensions × bits; every cell gets a distinct key from 0 to 2^(dimensions × bits) − 1. Values outside the bounds are clamped to the edge cells; NaN is an error. Up to 64 bits for 1–2 dimensions, 32 for 3–4, 16 for 5–8 and 8 for 9–16. A GEOMETRY value with 2-D bounds is encoded by the centre of its bounding box; empty geometries give NULL.

examples.description: Quantize a point in a 100 × 100 area to 16 bits per axis
Encode the centre of a geometry's bounding box

name: hilbert_decode_bounded
description: Decode a key from hilbert_encode_bounded with the same bounds and bits into the centre of its grid cell, as a DOUBLE array. The result is within half a cell of the encoded value.

examples.description: Recover the cell centre

name: hilbert_encode_latlon
description: Encode a latitude/longitude pair with the Hilbert curve over a grid of 2^bits cells per axis. The default of 32 bits gives a UBIGINT key; 16 bits gives a UINTEGER. Latitude must be within [-90, 90] and longitude within [-180, 180]. Equivalent to hilbert_encode_bounded([lat, lon], [-90, -180], [90, 180], bits).

examples.description: Encode a location with the default 32 bits per axis
Use 16 bits per axis for a smaller key

name: hilbert_decode_latlon
description: Decode a key from hilbert_encode_latlon with the same bits (default 32) into the centre of its grid cell, as STRUCT(lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE).

examples.description: Round-trip a location

name: hilbert_ranges
description: Table function returning the sorted, disjoint key ranges (lo, hi) of hilbert_encode that cover the box between min_point and max_point. The points are arrays of the encoded type. The cover is exact until max_ranges (default 64) is reached, then a superset that never misses a key in the box. Intended for systems that store or index only the key; inside DuckDB, a coordinate filter on key-sorted data is faster.

examples.description: Ranges covering a small box
Cap the number of ranges; the cover then includes some keys outside the box
examples.code: SELECT count(*) AS ranges, sum(hi - lo + 1) AS keys FROM hilbert_ranges([2, 3]::UTINYINT[2], [100, 120]::UTINYINT[2], 4);

name: hilbert_ranges_bounded
description: Table function returning the key ranges (lo, hi) of hilbert_encode_bounded, with the given bounds and bits, that cover the box between min_point and max_point. Exact at grid-cell resolution until max_ranges (default 64) is reached, then a superset; filter fetched rows on their coordinates.

examples.description: At most 8 ranges for a box on a 256 × 256 grid

name: morton_encode
description: Encode coordinates into one unsigned integer by interleaving their bits (Morton / Z-order). Accepts the same types, dimensions and argument forms as hilbert_encode. Keys sort like the coordinates, including negative and floating-point values.

examples.description: Order nonnegative integer coordinates by their Morton (Z-order) curve key
Pass coordinates as separate arguments, including negative values
Encode two dates
